reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Piloting UN national AI strategy blueprint
themes.definition: Speaker reports its own national AI and data strategy, here as first pilot of a UN blueprint, and offers to share lessons toward digital sovereignty.
themes.inclusion: Include passages describing the country's national AI strategy design or implementation.
themes.exclusion: Exclude generic support for AI innovation without a national policy or programme.
themes.boundary_cases: Where the strategy is UN-supported, also code AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: As the first member state to pilot the UN Blueprint for National AI and Data Strategies from design into national implementation

themes.label: Global Fund for AI capacity building
themes.definition: Support for international instruments that fund AI capacity building so AI is shared equitably among nations.
themes.inclusion: Include references to AI capacity-building funds, technology sharing or support to developing countries.
themes.exclusion: Exclude domestic digital infrastructure without international support framing.
themes.boundary_cases: Equitable sharing framed as an access gap may also be AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: contribute our experience to emerging instruments such as the proposed Global Fund for AI capacity building

themes.label: Safety, privacy and accountability concerns
themes.definition: While welcoming AI, speakers raise threats to safety, privacy, accountability and retained human agency and control.
themes.inclusion: Include passages flagging rights, privacy, safety or accountability concerns about AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages framing risk solely as military or cyber threats.
themes.boundary_cases: Concern that AI outpaces governance capacity while retaining human control could also be AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL if catastrophic risk is invoked; here it is framed as accountability.

examples.quote: we should not lose sight of the need to address clear threats to people’s rights to safety and privacy
This raises critical questions regarding accountability, safety, environmental, impact

themes.label: Opportunities outpacing governance capacity
themes.definition: AI is framed as offering enormous opportunities yet advancing faster than the capacity to govern it, including risk of a widening divide.
themes.inclusion: Include explicit pairings of AI opportunities with governance or equity risks.
themes.boundary_cases: The widening divide element may also be coded AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: artificial intelligence, are advancing faster than our current capacity to govern them while retaining human agency and control
The transformation brought about by digitalization and artificial intelligence presents enormous opportunities for humanity.

themes.label: Exclusion from shaping and benefiting from AI
themes.definition: Concern about a digital divide between those who shape AI and those excluded, and rural lack of digital access.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on unequal access to or influence over AI and digital tools.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages on generic poverty without technology link.
themes.boundary_cases: Rural digital access gaps without AI mention are generic digitalization and should be coded only when tied to AI in the same passage.

examples.quote: the risk of a widening digital divide between those who can shape these technologies and those who are excluded from their benefits

value.rationale: Southern African passages welcome AI but stress accountability, privacy and equity; Lesotho 2026 is distinctive in reporting national AI strategy implementation under a UN blueprint and backing an AI capacity-building fund.
